questions.stem: The RN is caring for four clients. Which task is most appropriate to delegate to an unregulated care provider (UCP/PSW)?
options: Teaching a newly diagnosed diabetic client how to use an insulin pen
Ambulating a stable client on post-op day 2 after knee surgery
Performing the admission assessment for a client with chest pain
Evaluating a client's response to IV morphine
questions.rationale: UCPs can do routine tasks for stable clients with predictable outcomes. Assessment, teaching and evaluation stay with the RN.

questions.stem: After receiving report, which client should the nurse see first?
options: Client with COPD whose SpO₂ is 90% on 2 L/min
Client 1 hour post-op who received morphine and now has RR 8/min and is difficult to rouse
Client with a pressure injury requesting a dressing change
Client with diabetes whose pre-lunch glucose is 9 mmol/L (162 mg/dL)
questions.rationale: RR 8 and decreased level of consciousness after an opioid is a breathing problem and possible opioid toxicity: ABCs first. SpO₂ 90% is often an acceptable target for a client with COPD.

questions.stem: A client scheduled for surgery asks the nurse what the surgeon will be removing. What is the nurse's role regarding informed consent?
options: Explain the procedure in detail and have the client sign
Witness the client's signature and notify the surgeon that the client has questions
Tell the client the procedure is routine and to sign the form
Ask the family to sign on the client's behalf
questions.rationale: The provider explains the procedure, risks and alternatives. The nurse witnesses the signature and advocates by notifying the provider when the client does not understand.

questions.stem: Which actions by a nurse protect client confidentiality? Select all that apply.
options: Logging off the computer when leaving the workstation
Discussing a client's diagnosis in the elevator with a coworker
Giving information only to people the client has authorized
Posting a photo of a 'cool wound' on social media without the name
Using the minimum necessary information when giving report
questions.rationale: Lock screens, authorized disclosure only, and minimum necessary info all protect privacy. Public conversations and social media posts are breaches, even without a name.

questions.stem: A competent adult client with a valid DNR order goes into cardiac arrest. The daughter shouts, 'Do everything!' What should the nurse do?
options: Start CPR because the family requests it
Follow the DNR order and support the daughter
Call the provider to cancel the DNR
Start CPR until the provider arrives
questions.rationale: A valid advance directive from a competent client must be honoured. The nurse advocates for the client's wishes and gives emotional support to the family.

questions.stem: A client is diagnosed with Clostridioides difficile. Which hand hygiene is required after care?
questions.rationale: C. difficile spores are not killed by alcohol. Use contact precautions and wash with soap and water to remove the spores physically.

questions.stem: A nurse discovers a fire in a client's room. Using RACE, what is the FIRST action?
options: Contain the fire by closing the door
Rescue the client from immediate danger
questions.rationale: Rescue → Alarm → Contain → Extinguish/Evacuate. For the extinguisher, remember PASS: Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep.

questions.stem: A client has a prescribed wrist restraint. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Tie the restraint to the bed frame
Tie the restraint to the side rail
Check circulation and skin regularly per policy (at least every 2 hours)
Use a PRN restraint order for convenience
questions.rationale: Tie to the frame (side rails move and can injure), use quick-release knots, and monitor circulation, skin and needs. Restraint orders are never PRN.

questions.stem: A client with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis is admitted. Which precautions should the nurse implement?
options: Airborne: N95 respirator and negative-pressure room
questions.rationale: TB, measles and varicella are airborne: fit-tested N95 and a negative-pressure (AIIR) room. The client wears a surgical mask when outside the room.

questions.stem: A parent asks when their baby's weight should triple. The nurse answers:
questions.rationale: Birth weight doubles by about 6 months and triples by about 12 months.

questions.stem: One hour after delivery, the nurse finds a boggy uterus above the umbilicus with heavy lochia. What is the FIRST action?
options: Have the client empty her bladder
questions.rationale: A boggy uterus means uterine atony, the leading cause of postpartum hemorrhage. Massage the fundus first. Then assess the bladder (a full bladder displaces the uterus) and notify the provider if it stays boggy.

questions.stem: Which vaccine is contraindicated during pregnancy?
questions.rationale: MMR is a live vaccine and is avoided in pregnancy. Inactivated flu and Tdap are recommended in pregnancy.

questions.stem: A client says, 'I don't think I'll ever get better.' Which response is most therapeutic?
options: 'You sound discouraged. Tell me more about that.'
'You should talk to your doctor about this.'
questions.rationale: Reflecting feelings and using open-ended prompts is therapeutic. False reassurance, 'why' questions (which feel judgmental) and passing the buck are non-therapeutic.

questions.stem: A client with heavy alcohol use was admitted 48 hours ago and is now tremulous, confused and hallucinating, with HR 124. The nurse anticipates which priority medication?
questions.rationale: These are signs of severe withdrawal / possible delirium tremens (usually 48–72 h). Benzodiazepines are first-line. Also start seizure precautions and give thiamine.

questions.stem: A client taking lithium has a level of 2.0 mEq/L. Which findings would the nurse expect? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Therapeutic level is ~0.6–1.2 mEq/L. Toxicity causes coarse tremor, GI upset and neuro changes. A fine tremor is a common side effect at therapeutic levels.

questions.stem: A client with depression who has been withdrawn suddenly seems calm and is giving away personal belongings. What is the nurse's priority?
options: Directly assess the client for suicidal thoughts and plan
Tell the client the change is a good sign
questions.rationale: A sudden calm and giving things away are warning signs. Ask directly about suicidal ideation, plan and means, and maintain safety per policy.

questions.stem: Which intervention best prevents pressure injuries in an immobile client?
options: Keep the head of bed at 60° at all times
questions.rationale: Regular repositioning relieves pressure. Never massage reddened areas, avoid donut cushions, and keep the HOB at or below 30° when possible to reduce shear.

questions.stem: A client is learning to go UP stairs with crutches. Which instruction is correct?
options: Crutches first, then the good leg
Good (unaffected) leg first, then crutches and affected leg
questions.rationale: 'Up with the good, down with the bad.' Going up: the strong leg leads. Going down: crutches and the affected leg lead.

questions.stem: A client on a low-sodium diet chooses lunch. Which choice shows understanding?
options: Fresh grilled chicken with steamed vegetables
questions.rationale: Canned, cured, pickled and instant foods are high in sodium. Fresh, unprocessed foods are best.

questions.stem: Before giving digoxin, the nurse finds an apical pulse of 54/min. What should the nurse do?
options: Give the dose and recheck in 1 hour
Hold the dose and notify the provider
questions.rationale: Hold digoxin if the apical HR is below 60 in an adult (count for a full minute), and report it. Also watch for toxicity: nausea, vision changes (yellow-green halos), and low potassium, which increases toxicity.

questions.stem: Which medication is the antidote for heparin?
questions.rationale: Heparin → protamine sulfate (monitor aPTT). Warfarin → vitamin K (monitor INR). Naloxone reverses opioids, flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines.

questions.stem: The order is amoxicillin 250 mg PO. Available: 125 mg/5 mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
questions.rationale: Desired ÷ Have × Volume = 250 ÷ 125 × 5 mL = 10 mL.

questions.stem: Which statement about IV potassium chloride is correct?
options: It may be given IV push if the client is hypokalemic
It must always be diluted and given by infusion, never IV push
It can be given faster in emergencies by IV push
It does not require cardiac monitoring at any rate
questions.rationale: Never give potassium by IV push: it can cause fatal dysrhythmias. Always dilute, infuse with a pump, and check urine output and the IV site.

questions.stem: Which insulin facts are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Regular insulin can be given IV
Glargine (long-acting) can be mixed with other insulins
When mixing, draw up clear (regular) before cloudy (NPH)
Rapid-acting (lispro) is given with or just before meals
Hypoglycemia signs include sweating, shakiness, and confusion
questions.rationale: Regular insulin is the IV insulin. Clear before cloudy. Glargine is never mixed. Rapid-acting insulin goes with meals. Hypoglycemia causes shaky, sweaty, confused behaviour: treat with 15 g fast carbs.

questions.stem: Ten minutes into a blood transfusion, the client reports back pain and chills; temperature rises. The nurse's FIRST action is:
options: Stop the transfusion and keep the line open with normal saline using new tubing
questions.rationale: Suspected hemolytic reaction: stop the transfusion first, keep the IV open with NS on new tubing, then notify the provider and blood bank and send the bag and tubing.

questions.stem: A client's potassium is 6.2 mEq/L. What is the nurse's priority action?
options: Place the client on a cardiac monitor
questions.rationale: Hyperkalemia can cause peaked T waves and fatal dysrhythmias. Monitor the heart and notify the provider; treatment may include calcium gluconate, insulin + dextrose, and binders.

questions.stem: After a cardiac catheterization through the femoral artery, which action is the priority?
options: Check distal pulses and the insertion site for bleeding
Flex the affected leg to improve comfort
questions.rationale: Watch for bleeding/hematoma and impaired circulation: check site, pulses, colour, temperature. Keep the leg straight for the prescribed time, and encourage fluids to flush the contrast.

questions.stem: After a thyroidectomy, the client reports tingling around the mouth. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Perioral tingling, Chvostek's and Trousseau's signs mean hypocalcemia. Keep IV calcium gluconate and a tracheostomy set available.

questions.stem: A client is 6 hours post abdominal surgery. For each finding, mark whether it needs FOLLOW-UP or is EXPECTED.

rows.text: Urine output 15 mL/h for the past 2 h

questions.rationale: Low BP + high HR + low urine output + restlessness + pallor all point to possible hemorrhage / hypovolemic shock. Mild pain and hypoactive bowel sounds are expected early after abdominal surgery.

questions.stem: ABG: pH 7.30, PaCO₂ 52 mmHg, HCO₃⁻ 24 mEq/L. Interpret.
questions.rationale: pH low = acidosis. PaCO₂ high (matches) = respiratory. HCO₃⁻ normal = uncompensated. Tip: ROME, Respiratory Opposite, Metabolic Equal.

questions.stem: A client arrives with diabetic ketoacidosis (glucose 32 mmol/L, Kussmaul respirations). What is the FIRST priority intervention?
questions.rationale: DKA causes severe dehydration: fluids first (0.9% NS). Then a regular insulin infusion, with close potassium monitoring, because insulin moves K⁺ into cells.

questions.stem: A client develops hives, wheezing and throat tightness after an antibiotic. The FIRST medication is:
questions.rationale: Anaphylaxis: IM epinephrine (anterolateral thigh) first. Stop the drug and maintain the airway. Antihistamines and steroids are add-ons.

questions.stem: A client presents with sudden right-sided weakness and slurred speech that began 1 hour ago. Before thrombolytics, which test is essential?
options: Non-contrast CT scan of the head
questions.rationale: A CT rules out a hemorrhagic stroke. Thrombolytics (tPA) would be fatal in a bleed. Time matters: 'time is brain.'

questions.stem: A client has heart failure. Mark each instruction INDICATED or NOT INDICATED for discharge teaching.

rows.text: Weigh yourself every morning at the same time
Drink at least 3 litres of fluid daily
Report a gain of ~1 kg (2 lb) in a day or 2 kg (5 lb) in a week

questions.rationale: Daily weights, reporting rapid gain, and sodium restriction manage fluid. HF clients often need fluid restriction, and usually breathe easier with the head elevated.
